payload.rationale: The 30-year fixed mortgage rate has shown a consistent upward trend over the past month, rising from 6.65% on August 20 to 6.95% on September 17. The most recent weekly increase was substantial at 19 basis points. To resolve 'Yes', the rate must increase by more than 6 basis points (to >7.01%) in the September 24 report. While a 7 basis point increase is well within typical weekly volatility, assuming a random walk with zero drift places the probability of such an increase around 30-40%. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that the recent 19 basis point jump might be an overreaction to specific economic news, leading to stabilization or mean reversion in the following week. The strongest reason this could be too low is if the macroeconomic factors driving the recent sharp increase persist, maintaining strong upward momentum that easily pushes the rate past the 7.01% threshold.
limitations: Only five recent weekly observations are provided, lacking broader context on bond yields or specific macroeconomic drivers.
Weekly mortgage rate changes can be highly volatile and are difficult to predict without real-time daily Treasury yield data.
